simple.meaning: נָשַׂק (nâsaq) is a Hebrew word meaning “to catch fire.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: נָשַׂק (H5400) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Psalms 78:21, with occurrences in Psalms, Isaiah, Ezekiel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נָשַׂק (H5400) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in נָשַׂק (H5400) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: נָשַׂק (nâsaq) / H5400 is traced through Psalms 78:21, Isaiah 44:15, Ezekiel 39:9 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H5400. nasaq [ שָׂלִק ] verb kindle, burn (Ecclus 43:4 margin הִסִּיק , Neh 7:21 ; 7:23 הִשִּׂיק , burn ; Aramaic (also BA) סְלַק ascend , Aph`el cause to go up (in flame), offer sacrifice; , Palmyrene סלק ascend ); — Niph`al Perfect 3feminine singular בְיַעֲקֹב נִשְּׂקָה אֵשׁ Psa 78:21 a fire was kindled against Jacob. Hiph`il make a fire burn: Perfect 3plural consecutive וְהִשִּׂיקוּ , with ב of thing; Imperfect 3masculine singular absolute יְשִּׂיק Isa 44:15 (both || בִּעֵר ).
